title: Security scans of public sites
summary: Concept for making security scans of publicly hosted sites a first-class Quality Studio review kind. Three layers: the outside view (TLS, headers, cookies, DNS, short port list, exposed files, served secrets) runs for every site with a token proof. Safe active checks (Nuclei, ZAP baseline crawl) and agent-driven review (access control, auth/session, API abuse with test accounts) need explicit, expiring switches. Recommends the lean tool set T1 (native checks, testssl.sh, Gitleaks, then Nuclei, then ZAP as an optional image; skip Nmap, sslyze, Nikto, sqlmap and hosted scanners; defer Trivy/Grype) in one pull-based scanner-worker image, first beside Quality Studio and later on an external vantage host. Evidence lives in a restricted data-root area that never reaches a checkout, an export or logs. Live sites become QS-SITE boundaries in the attack coverage matrix, a versioned site prompt library turns raw hits into judged findings, and Agent Studio triggers scans from deploy reconciliation and receives a redacted summary, cards and, after an advisory period, a promotion gate. Eleven slices across Quality Studio and Agent Studio; slice 1 runs all outside-view checks, including served-content secrets, on one registered site and shows its findings.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Outside-view scan of one registered site
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Site registry with token proof, pull-based scanner worker image, all L0 checks with testssl.sh and Gitleaks over served content, normalisation into ReviewFinding, restricted evidence store, CLI/API and a minimal Sites view. No Agent Studio change.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 1 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- Site registry at `<base>/sites/<site-key>/site.json` (hostnames, owning repository registration, declared operator addresses, switches). Directories are created with mode 0700 and are outside every project directory.
- Ownership proof: issue a random token on registration and verify either a DNS TXT record at `_qs-site-verification.<host>` or `https://<host>/.well-known/qs-site-verification/<token-id>`. Re-check before a scan when the last proof is older than 24 h. A failed check gives status `unverified`, never clean.
- Scanner worker image `quality-site-scanner`: a separate Dockerfile with testssl.sh pinned by release tag and SHA-256 (verified at build), Gitleaks reused from the existing pin, non-root, read-only root filesystem, no mounts. The worker claims jobs with a worker token (`POST /api/site-scans/claim`) and posts results back. Quality Studio never connects to the worker.
- L0 checks from the Dossier's outside-view table (TLS via testssl.sh JSON; headers, cookies, redirects, disclosure, exposed-file list with content signatures, CORS probe, DNS, short port list, security.txt natively, plus served-content secrets with Gitleaks). Exact verified hostnames only. Refuse loopback, link-local, private and metadata addresses (the test seam is not configurable in production). Skip port probes for addresses not owned by the operator and record `omitted`. Budget ≤ 300 requests and ≤ 2 req/s. Back off on 429 and 503, and abort on target distress.
- For the served-content check, fetch the start page, same-host scripts and stylesheets it references, and their declared source maps into an ephemeral directory. Cap collection at 25 files and 20 MiB total. Run the pinned `gitleaks dir` with the existing redaction; emit `site/served-secret` (high) at the asset URL through the `site-served-secrets` sensor. Never fetch an asset on another host. A failed Gitleaks run is unavailable, never clean; a cap hit makes the scan incomplete with recorded omissions. Delete the temporary content after normalisation.
- Normalise into `ReviewFinding` with `site://host:port/path` locations, `FindingSource(Deterministic, "site-outside-view" or "site-served-secrets", producer, version)` and stable fingerprints. Write scan provenance (worker, vantage label, egress address, image digest, tool versions, resolved addresses, proof id, request count, `complete`, omissions).
- CLI `quality site register|verify|scan`, API `PUT /api/sites/{siteKey}`, `POST /api/sites/{siteKey}/verify`, `POST /api/sites/{siteKey}/scans`, `GET /api/sites/{siteKey}/scans/{scanId}`. A minimal **Sites** view next to the Security matrix button lists the sites, the proof state, the last scan and its findings.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. A fixture site in the test suite (planted: missing HSTS, served `/.git/HEAD` with a valid signature, `Server` version header, a cookie without `Secure`, plus an expired self-signed certificate on a second fixture) yields exactly the expected rule ids. A clean fixture yields zero findings with `complete: true`.
2. An unverified host gets no request beyond the proof check, as the fixture request log shows. A host that resolves to a private address is refused.
3. The fixture request log shows ≤ 300 requests, ≤ 2 req/s and only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. The scan finishes in ≤ 5 minutes.
4. A missing or failing testssl.sh or Gitleaks gives `available: false` for its respective check and never a clean result.
5. A fixture bundle with a Gitleaks test key yields one redacted `site/served-secret` finding at the asset URL; the secret value appears in no stored file or log. The fixture request log shows no fetches from another host. A 25-file or 20 MiB cap hit sets `complete: false` with omissions.
6. Nothing is written under any registered checkout. `quality report` and the JSON exports contain no site findings. A log-capture test finds no finding title, path or excerpt in the logs.
7. One real operator site, registered by token proof, is scanned from the worker. The card result reports only the scan id, `complete` and counts by severity. Light and dark screenshots of the Sites view use the fixture site.
8. The scanner image size and every tool digest are recorded in the card result.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Site evidence access, retention and redaction
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: CanReadSiteSecurity client flag, site-to-registration binding, export exclusion, 90-day raw-output retention, excerpt redaction, redacted card handover.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 2 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slice 1 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- Hosted mode: add `CanReadSiteSecurity` to the API client options next to `CanRegisterRepositories`. Site routes require it plus access to the site's owning repository registration and answer 404 otherwise. Local mode is unchanged.
- Retention: delete raw tool output under `scans/<scan-id>/raw/` after 90 days (configurable). Keep normalised findings and lifecycle.
- Redaction: excerpts are limited to the status, the relevant headers and at most 2 KiB of body after Gitleaks redaction. Credentials and tokens never appear.
- `AgentStudioTaskClient` handover for site findings sends a redacted title (severity, environment, project) and a Quality Studio link only. Add `--include-site-findings` to `quality report`, refusing any output path inside a registered checkout.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. API tests: a client without the flag, or without repository access, gets 404 on every site route. A client with both gets 200.
2. A retention test with a clock seam deletes raw output after 90 days and keeps the findings.
3. A fixture response containing a Gitleaks test secret is stored redacted.
4. The dry-run card payload for a site finding contains no URL path, payload or finding title.
5. `--include-site-findings` with an output path inside a checkout fails with a clear error.

implementationTasks.title: [Agent Studio] Register hosted sites and request scans on deploy
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Reconciliation step that registers stage/production sites with Quality Studio, places the proof file on the edge, requests L0 scans idempotently, and shows advisory status on the deploy-run drawer, environment card and Security rail.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 3 (target project: **Agent Studio**) from the site-security-scans Dossier. Quality Studio slices 1 and 2 must exist.

Source: Quality Studio repository, docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Use its working decisions unless it records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule:** never copy site finding titles, paths or payloads into Agent Studio cards, logs, commits or card results. Agent Studio holds a redacted summary and a Quality Studio link only.

**Build**
- After `DeploymentReconciler.Reconcile` in `DeployService.SyncLocked`, select succeeded deployments of `stage` or `production` environments that have `Hosting.Domains`. Register or update each site in Quality Studio (`PUT /api/sites/{siteKey}`), using only domains that passed `RunTargetDomainSuffixes` and `ClaimDomains`.
- On the first public deployment, have the edge serve the Quality Studio proof file at `/.well-known/qs-site-verification/<token-id>`. Agent Studio does not claim ownership itself.
- Request an L0 scan (`POST /api/sites/{siteKey}/scans`) with `layer`, `reason` (`first-public` or `deploy`), `deploymentId`, `releaseId`, `commitSha` and `environmentId`. The idempotency key is the deployment id plus the layer. For `Edge: cloudflare`, mark port probes omitted.
- Show the advisory summary (status, age, counts by severity, link) in `DeployRunDrawerComponent`, `DeployEnvironmentCardComponent` and the project Security rail (`SecurityPanelComponent`). Nothing blocks.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. An integration test with a fake Quality Studio: one succeeded production deployment produces exactly one registration and one scan request, and a repeated reconciliation produces none.
2. A domain outside `RunTargetDomainSuffixes` is never registered.
3. A failed or cancelled deployment requests no scan.
4. The summary shown in the UI contains no finding title or path, as a component test checks. Light and dark screenshots of the three surfaces use the fake data.
5. An unreachable Quality Studio leaves the deployment state unchanged and records the request for retry.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Scheduled scans and site finding lifecycle
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Quality Studio-owned schedule (L0 daily, L1 weekly when switched on), lifecycle resolution on absence in complete scans, regression flag against the previous scan, redacted summary endpoint.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 4 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slice 1 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- A `BackgroundService` scheduler with a `PeriodicTimer`, following the existing hosted-service pattern. It runs L0 daily per verified site and L1 weekly when its switch is on and not expired. A global kill switch and a kill switch per site stop running jobs within 10 s.
- Lifecycle in `sites/<site-key>/findings/state.json`: a finding absent from a *complete* scan of the same layer becomes resolved. An incomplete scan resolves nothing. A finding that reappears reopens with its history.
- Regression: mark findings that are new against the previous complete scan of the same layer.
- `GET /api/sites/{siteKey}/scans/{scanId}/summary` returns the scan id, layer, status, `complete`, counts by severity, the new-finding count and the vantage label, with no titles or paths.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. With a clock seam, a site gets exactly one L0 scan per day, and L1 only while the switch is valid.
2. A fixture whose weakness is fixed between two complete scans shows the finding resolved. With an incomplete second scan it stays open.
3. The kill switch stops a running fixture scan within 10 s.
4. A contract test confirms that the summary has no finding text.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Site boundaries in the attack coverage matrix
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: site-inventory.v1 schema and writer, QS-SITE-* catalogue entries, applicability extension of existing entries, site ledger, deploymentChanged staleness, source filter and code-to-site route linkage in the matrix.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 5 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slice 1 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- Schema `schemas/site-inventory.v1.schema.json`, written to `sites/<site-key>/inventory.json`, with kinds `site-origin`, `site-route`, `site-api-operation`, `site-auth-flow`, `site-dns` and `site-port`. Each fact carries `derivedFrom` evidence or `unknown`.
- Catalogue entries `QS-SITE-TLS`, `QS-SITE-HEADERS`, `QS-SITE-COOKIES`, `QS-SITE-EXPOSED-FILES`, `QS-SITE-DNS` and `QS-SITE-PORTS`, with `deterministicRuleIds` for the `site/*` rules and conclusive in both directions like `QS-CONTROL-*`. Extend the applicability of `OWASP-API8`, `OWASP-API9`, `OWASP-API1`, `OWASP-API5`, `OWASP-A01`, `OWASP-API2`, `SESSION-CSRF` and `AUTH-BRUTE-FORCE` as the Dossier lists.
- Site ledger `sites/<site-key>/attacks/coverage-ledger.jsonl` with the existing append-only contract. New staleness reasons are `deploymentChanged` and `siteInventoryChanged`.
- In the matrix view, a source filter (code, site, both) and a link between a `site-route` and the code boundary with the matching route template when the site's repository is registered.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. For an L0-only fixture site, every `QS-SITE-*` cell is `pass` or `finding`, and every broad OWASP cell is `notYetChecked`.
2. Recording a new deployed commit marks the site cells stale with `deploymentChanged`, and code cells are unchanged.
3. The catalogue and schema tests pass, and the existing matrix tests are unchanged.
4. Light and dark screenshots of the matrix filtered to the fixture site.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Safe active checks with Nuclei
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: site-templates sensor: pinned Nuclei binary and template commit in the worker image, tag policy, rate limits, L1 switch with expiry and audit.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 6 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slices 1 and 4 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- Add Nuclei to `quality-site-scanner`, pinned by binary SHA-256 and template commit, with the update check disabled. Templates change only when the image is rebuilt.
- Policy: HTTP, SSL and DNS templates only. Exclude the tags `intrusive`, `dos`, `fuzz` and `default-login`, code and headless templates, and DAST mode. ≤ 2,000 requests, ≤ 5 req/s, concurrency ≤ 2.
- The L1 switch per site records who set it, the reason and an expiry (default 90 days) in an audit log. Without a valid switch, no L1 job is created.
- Hits are normalised as observations. Only templates that the site rule pack marks conclusive become findings directly. The others wait for triage (slice 9).

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Against a fixture with one planted known exposure, the matching template fires, and the request log shows only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and stays within budget.
2. A template carrying an excluded tag in a fixture template set never runs.
3. An expired switch stops scheduled L1 jobs.
4. The provenance records the Nuclei version and the template commit.

implementationTasks.title: [Agent Studio] Scan credentials from the secret provider
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Workload grant that lets the scan worker resolve secret:// references scoped to one project/environment at job start; audit; no value exposure.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 7 (target project: **Agent Studio**) from the site-security-scans Dossier. Slice 3 must exist.

Source: Quality Studio repository, docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Use its working decisions unless it records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule:** never copy site finding titles, paths or payloads into Agent Studio cards, logs, commits or card results. Agent Studio holds a redacted summary and a Quality Studio link only.

**Build**
- A workload identity for the Quality Studio scan worker and a remote resolution endpoint backed by `ISecretProvider.GetForWorkloadAsync`. It resolves only `secret://<project>/<environment>/<name>` references bound for that environment, and a production binding needs `ApprovedBy` as in `ProjectSecretBindings`.
- Each resolution is audited with the worker id, the scan id and the reference, never the value. Grants are short-lived (≤ 1 h) and are bound to the scan id that Quality Studio issues.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. The worker resolves a staging test account and is refused for another project, another environment, or an unbound name.
2. A production reference without `ApprovedBy` is refused.
3. A log-capture test shows no secret value anywhere. The audit log has one entry per resolution.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Crawl and authenticated crawl with ZAP baseline
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Optional quality-site-scanner-zap image, site-crawl sensor with passive rules only, authenticated crawl with a test account by secret reference, crawl map into the site inventory.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 8 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slices 6 and 7 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- A separate optional image `quality-site-scanner-zap`, pinned by digest, that claims only `site-crawl` jobs.
- An automation-framework plan with the spider (bounded time, ≤ 2,000 requests, ≤ 5 req/s) and passive scan only, with no active scan. The authenticated variant logs in with a test account resolved through slice 7. The credential is kept only in process memory.
- Passive alerts become observations for triage. The crawl map feeds `site-route` entries in the site inventory.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Against a fixture with a login-protected area, the authenticated crawl discovers routes that the anonymous crawl does not.
2. The request log shows no state-changing method and no request outside the verified host.
3. The credential value appears in no stored file or log.
4. The image size is recorded, and the main worker image is unchanged.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Triage of tool hits into judged findings
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: site-hit-triage.v1 prompt, triage runner with scoped confirming GET, two judgements for high/critical, false-positive memory per fingerprint.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 9 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slices 5 and 6 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- Prompt `prompts/site-hit-triage.v1.md`. Site content is untrusted and goes between the existing content-boundary markers. The output is `confirmed`, `false-positive` or `needs-human`, with evidence and the matching catalogue entry. The prompt runs with `ReviewerIsolation` clean context.
- The runner allows at most one confirming GET through the worker's scoped HTTP tool. High and critical results need two independent agent/model/thinking identities. Contradictions keep the conservative result and set `needsHumanAttention`.
- A false positive is stored against the fingerprint with the model and prompt hash, and is re-triaged only when the template or the deployed commit changes.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. On recorded fixture hits (5 true and 5 false), the runner with a fake agent records the verdicts, and confirmed hits become findings linked to matrix cells.
2. A fixture page containing an instruction aimed at the agent is treated as data. A test asserts that the instruction is quoted inside the markers.
3. A false positive is not triaged again on an unchanged rescan.
4. Token usage per triage is recorded in the usage ledger.

implementationTasks.title: [Quality Studio] Agent-driven site review with test accounts
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Scoped HTTP tool with credential injection by role, method policy and budget; prompts site-reconnaissance, auth-session, access-control, api-abuse and site-attack-coverage v1; L2 switch per site and environment.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 10 (target project: **Quality Studio**) from docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Slices 7 and 9 must exist.

Use the working decisions in docs/site-security-scans/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule (applies to every slice):** the repository is public. Never commit, attach to card results, log or screenshot findings of a real site. Public evidence uses the local fixture sites only. A real-site run is reported as counts and scan id only.

**Build**
- The scoped HTTP tool in the worker enforces the verified hostnames, a method policy per site (state-changing methods only for a test tenant), ≤ 1,500 requests per run and ≤ 2 req/s. It logs in by role name with accounts resolved through slice 7, so the agent never sees a credential. Every exchange is recorded as redacted evidence.
- Prompts `site-reconnaissance.v1`, `site-auth-session-review.v1`, `site-access-control-review.v1`, `site-api-abuse-review.v1` and `site-attack-coverage-review.v1`, with the same untrusted-content markers and reviewer isolation.
- The L2 switch is per site and environment, defaults to staging, and covers production only when production is named. It has an expiry and is audited.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. On a fixture app with two roles and a planted horizontal access flaw, the access-control run reports it with recorded exchanges and fills the matching `OWASP-API1-BOLA` cell.
2. The tool refuses requests to another host, forbidden methods, and requests over budget, and a test proves each refusal.
3. No credential value appears in a prompt, transcript, evidence file or log.
4. Without a valid switch, no L2 job starts.

implementationTasks.title: [Agent Studio] Site security cards and deploy gate
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Redacted cards for new high/critical site findings, site-security verdict input to the release-candidate gate in advisory then blocking stages, override with reason and expiry.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement slice 11 (target project: **Agent Studio**) from the site-security-scans Dossier. Quality Studio slices 2 and 4 and Agent Studio slice 3 must exist.

Source: Quality Studio repository, docs/site-security-scans/index.html. Use its working decisions unless it records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Sensitivity rule:** never copy site finding titles, paths or payloads into Agent Studio cards, logs, commits or card results. Agent Studio holds a redacted summary and a Quality Studio link only.

**Build**
- Cards: create a bug card through `TaskMutationService.CreateJob` for each new critical or high site finding. The slug id is derived from the Quality Studio fingerprint so the card is idempotent, and the redacted title and Quality Studio link follow the pattern of `HealthAlerts`. Suppress the certificate-expiry card while an environment-health TLS warning is active for the same environment.
- Gate: accept a site-security verdict keyed by project, environment and commit (modelled on the release-suite verdict and `PUT /api/runner/release-suite-verdicts`), and evaluate it in `ReleaseCandidateGate` with a policy mode: `advisory` (default), `stage1` (block on a conclusive critical L0 finding on the staging scan of the same commit), or `stage2` (also block on judged critical findings). An override needs a reason and an expiry and is audited.
- A post-deploy production scan creates cards only and never triggers a rollback.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. In `advisory` mode a critical verdict shows in the deploy-run drawer and blocks nothing. In `stage1` mode the same verdict blocks promotion, and an override with an expiry releases it.
2. A repeated summary creates no duplicate card, and no card text contains a URL path or payload.
3. An unavailable or incomplete scan is shown as unknown, neither pass nor block, and is listed in the gate result.
4. Light and dark screenshots of the gate result in the drawer use fake data.
